sections.h2: Why the county line matters in Erie
sections.html:
Erie is a home rule town that straddles two counties. It lies in the southwest corner of Weld County and the east edge of Boulder County, with about 58 percent of residents on the Weld side and 42 percent on the Boulder side. That split decides which county treasurer bills your property tax and which county clerk records your deed.

Look at your tax bill or the county parcel search first. Whether the house is in Weld or Boulder County tells you who to call for a tax payoff figure and where the sale paperwork will be filed.

The town has two ZIP codes, 80514 and 80516, and sits roughly 25 minutes from Denver and 20 minutes from Boulder. Broomfield borders it to the south and Lafayette to the southwest.

Erie grew 65.6 percent between the 2010 and 2020 censuses, from roughly 18,100 residents to 30,038, and the 2024 estimate is 38,594. Median household income is $99,804. With that pace, a large share of local homes are newer than in most Colorado towns.

Newer construction can mean fewer deferred repairs, but also more neighbors offering similar homes. Situations we hear about in fast-growing suburbs include:

  • homeowners who must relocate for work before a listing could reasonably wrap up
  • owners of an inherited house who live out of state
  • landlords tired of managing a rental from a distance
  • sellers carrying a mortgage on a house that needs a new roof, flooring or paint

A direct sale to a cash buyer skips showings, staging and financing contingencies, which is the main reason people in these situations ask about it.

Erie began as a coal town, and the old mining years left two things that matter to a seller. The first is house age. Homes near the original town center may carry old additions, older plumbing and electrical systems, and records that take more digging to assemble. Most local mines had closed by 1960, and the Eagle Mine shut in 1978.

The second is flooding. Major floods hit in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built around Coal Creek after the 1972 flood. If your lot is near the creek, expect a buyer or lender to ask about flood zone status. Find out your parcel's status before you list.

Average annual precipitation is 16.17 inches. May is the wettest month at 2.60 inches and January is the driest at 0.57 inches. Dry air does not mean low risk to the structure: roofs, gutters, decks and exterior paint take sun and wind year-round, and an older roof is one of the first things a buyer's inspector flags. A cash buyer prices a worn roof into the offer and does not ask you to replace it first.

On the Weld County side, taxes are due January 1 for the previous year and can be paid in full or in two halves.

Payment optionDue date
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Weld does not accept partial payments, and a postmark on or before the due date counts. Late interest rises by month: the first half picks up 1 percent in March and 6 percent by August. Pay online at weldtax.com, by mail to PO Box 458, Greeley, or in person at 1400 N 17th Avenue, Greeley.

sections.h2: If your parcel is on the Boulder side
sections.html: For a Boulder County parcel, the Boulder County Treasurer collects the tax, so confirm the figures with that office. In either county, the title company usually orders a certificate of taxes due and handles the proration at closing. Weld has a Certificate of Taxes Due request form on its treasurer pages.

sections.h2: Recording fee for a Colorado deed
sections.html: Colorado charges a documentary fee of one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed recorded for real property, with any partial $100 counted as a full one. The fee goes to the county clerk and recorder, and the statute sets no fee at or below $500. Who pays it is usually settled in the purchase contract, so read that line before you sign.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of an Erie house work?
sections.html:
The sequence is short, and you decide at each stage whether to go on.

  • You share the address, condition and your timing.
  • The buyer reviews the property and may visit it.
  • You receive an offer, and you can accept, counter or decline.
  • A title company runs the title search, orders tax figures and prepares the deed.
  • You sign, the deed is recorded with the county clerk where the parcel sits, and you are paid.

Without a lender there is no appraisal or loan approval to wait on, so the pace is set mostly by title work and your preferred closing date. We do not promise a price or a timeline before we see the house.

faqs.q: Which county is Erie, Colorado in?
faqs.a: Both. Erie lies mostly in southwest Weld County (about 58 percent of residents) and partly in eastern Boulder County (about 42 percent). Your tax bill shows which county covers your parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Erie house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. Homeowners can sell in current condition to a cash buyer without repairs, cleaning or staging. A worn roof or dated kitchen lowers the offer but does not block the sale.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax when an Erie house sells?
faqs.a: The title company usually prorates it between seller and buyer at closing based on a certificate of taxes due. Colorado bills taxes in arrears, so the seller typically owes a share for the months owned. Ask your title officer for the exact split.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed fee in Colorado?
faqs.a: The documentary fee is one cent per $100 of the sale price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when a deed is recorded. The contract decides which side pays it.

faqs.q: Does being near Coal Creek affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can. Erie had major floods in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built along Coal Creek afterward. Buyers and lenders may check flood zone status for homes near the creek, so find out your parcel's status before you sell.
